chunks: And in a narration of Ḥarīz:

When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered into ihram, Jibrīl عليه السلام came to him and said: “Command your companions to perform al-ʿajj and al-thajj. Al-ʿajj is raising the voice in the talbiyah, and al-thajj is the slaughtering of the sacrificial camels.”

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةِ: the pilgrim’s devotional proclamation beginning with labbayka
key_terms.الْعَجِّ: raising the voice with the talbiyah during pilgrimage
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrīl عليه السلام, the angel who brings divine revelation

ai.seo_question: What do al-ʿajj and al-thajj mean in the rites of hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith explains two important acts associated with hajj after entering ihram: raising the voice in the talbiyah and slaughtering sacrificial camels. It presents this guidance as conveyed to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله through Jibrīl عليه السلام, showing the ritual significance of these practices.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2579 - In a narration from Hariz:

"When the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) entered the state of Ihram, Archangel Jibril (as) came to him and said: 'Command your companions to perform al-'ajj and al-thajj. Al-'ajj is raising the voice with the Talbiyah, and al-thajj is the slaughtering of sacrificial camels.'"
